text: If you were hoping this morning's clear sky would hold, keep an eye to the northwest this afternoon. We're sitting at a pleasant 74 with light wind right now, but that shortwave the forecasters flagged is still on track, and scattered showers and thunderstorms should fire up as we head toward a high near 78. The models don't fully agree on just how wet it gets, the Euro's calling for rain essentially all afternoon while the American model and ICON see it more as a coin flip, so I'd call it a real chance rather than a lock. Any storm that does pop could be on the stronger side, gusty wind and small hail possible, so keep that in mind if you're out and about or on the water, where northwest wind builds to 10 to 15 knots this afternoon. Things quiet down this evening, with showers wrapping up by 7 or so and skies clearing out overnight. If you can, I'd get outdoor plans in either before early afternoon or hold off until this evening, and use the drier stretch to sneak in a walk while skies allow it.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST: BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Thursday! We saw a few showers and thunderstorms overnight, and we’ll hang onto the chance for more showers and thunderstorms through the day ahead. There could be a few hit-or-miss showers this morning, but I think the better chance of a few showers and thunderstorms will be this afternoon. I suspect once again that a thunderstorm or two could be on the stronger side potentially featuring gusty winds and maybe some small hail.
